beats.label: S1 · Stealing a dead woman's life
beats.text: Con artist Sarah watches her lookalike Beth Childs jump in front of a train and steps into her identity, draining her bank account to reclaim her daughter Kira.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the identity swap that pulls Sarah into Beth's world and every alliance that follows.

beats.label: S1 · They are clones
beats.text: German Katja is sniped in front of Sarah, and soccer mom Alison and biology grad Cosima meet her to reveal the truth: they are all identical clones being picked off.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the Clone Club and the premise that drives every future season.

beats.label: S1 · The killer is one of them
beats.text: The Christian assassin hunting the clones turns out to be another clone, feral Ukrainian Helena, who stabs Sarah and vanishes, protected by a group called the Proletheans.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the Prolethean faction and plants Helena as the recurring wildcard sister.

beats.label: S1 · Monitors in their beds
beats.text: The clones realise their partners are paid observers. Sarah confronts Beth's boyfriend Paul, and Alison begins to suspect her husband Donnie of watching her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reframes every domestic relationship as surveillance, setting up Paul and Donnie's later reveals.

beats.label: S1 · Dyad and Delphine's betrayal
beats.text: Cosima falls for grad student Delphine, who is secretly reporting to Dr. Aldous Leekie of the Dyad Institute, the neolutionist company running the science behind the clones.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Dyad, Leekie, and the Cosima–Delphine romance that anchors the science thread.

beats.label: S1 · Sisters by birth
beats.text: Sarah's birth mother Amelia reveals Sarah and Helena are twins carried by the same surrogate. Helena stabs Amelia dead, and Sarah shoots Helena in return.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Locks in the Sarah–Helena blood bond that shapes every future season and appears to close Helena's arc.

beats.label: S1 · Refusing to sign
beats.text: Cosima decodes a patent hidden in the clone genome: Dyad owns them. Sarah refuses to sign Rachel Duncan's contract and returns home to find Kira and Mrs. S gone.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names Rachel, establishes the patent stakes, and launches the season 2 kidnapping plot.

cliffhanger.text: Sarah has walked away from Dyad's offer and come home to a ransacked house — Kira and Mrs. S are missing, and Alison has already signed her life away to Leekie.
questions: Who took Kira and Mrs. S, Dyad or the Proletheans?
Now that Donnie is exposed as her monitor, what will Alison do?
Is Helena really dead after Sarah shot her?

characters.name: Sarah Manning
characters.line: British con artist and clone at the centre of everything, now on the run after refusing to sign with Dyad.

characters.name: Helena
characters.line: Feral Ukrainian clone raised by the Prolethean cult to kill her sisters, revealed to be Sarah's twin and shot by Sarah at season's end.

characters.name: Alison Hendrix
characters.line: Suburban clone who has just signed Dyad's contract and confirmed her husband Donnie is her monitor after watching neighbour Aynsley choke to death.

characters.name: Cosima Niehaus
characters.line: Scientist clone in a relationship with Delphine, now displaying the same respiratory illness that killed Katja.
characters.note: Decoded the patent hidden in their DNA.

characters.name: Kira
characters.line: Sarah's young daughter, the only known biological child of any clone, missing along with Mrs. S at the finale.

characters.name: Mrs. S (Siobhan Sadler)
characters.line: Sarah's tough foster mother with hidden UK contacts, protecting Kira and connected to Sarah's birth-mother network.

characters.name: Felix
characters.line: Sarah's artist foster brother and confidant, the only person she trusts across every scheme.

characters.name: Rachel Duncan
characters.line: Corporate 'Proclone' raised inside Dyad by the project's founders; wants Sarah and Kira signed and controlled.

characters.name: Dr. Aldous Leekie
characters.line: Public face of Dyad and the neolutionist movement pushing self-directed human evolution.

characters.name: Paul Dierden
characters.line: Beth's boyfriend, exposed as her monitor, now aware of the clones and answering to Rachel.

characters.name: Donnie Hendrix
characters.line: Alison's clueless-seeming husband, revealed in the final scene to be her Dyad monitor.

characters.name: Art Bell
characters.line: Beth's police partner who has figured out Sarah was impersonating her and is about to arrest her.

beats.label: S2 · Kira in the wind
beats.text: Believing Dyad has taken Kira, Sarah hunts Rachel down at Dyad only to learn Mrs. S faked the kidnapping herself to hide Kira from both Dyad and the Proletheans.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resets Mrs. S as a player with her own network and starts the Prolethean-vs-Dyad tug-of-war over Kira.

beats.label: S2 · Helena taken by new Proletheans
beats.text: Helena survives Sarah's shot and is captured by farmer Henrik Johanssen's Prolethean sect, who forcibly harvest her eggs to breed with her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Recasts the Proletheans under Henrik and sets up Helena's fertility as a plot engine.

beats.label: S2 · The founders and the cure
beats.text: Sarah tracks down Ethan Duncan, Rachel's presumed-dead adoptive father, who reveals the Leda project was hijacked from him by Leekie and holds the science that could cure Cosima.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the Duncan origin story and the cure MacGuffin that drives Cosima's storyline.

beats.label: S2 · Donnie kills Leekie
beats.text: Donnie learns Alison was right about the clones, confronts Leekie and accidentally shoots him dead; he and Alison bury the body and rebuild their marriage over the grave.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Leekie as antagonist, elevates Rachel, and pivots the Hendrixes into full accomplices.

beats.label: S2 · Helena burns down the farm
beats.text: Discovering Henrik plans to impregnate more women with her eggs, Helena kills him, torches the farm and reunites with Sarah, joining the clones as family.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends the Prolethean threat and turns Helena from villain into sister.

beats.label: S2 · Rachel steals Kira
beats.text: Rachel, gutted at learning she can never have children, poses as Sarah and abducts Kira. Sarah surrenders to Dyad, then shoots a pencil into Rachel's eye and escapes.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends Rachel's active leadership of Dyad and sets up her wounded, sidelined position for later.

beats.label: S2 · The Castor reveal
beats.text: Mrs. S and Paul hand Helena over to the military as a trade. Sarah then meets Dyad executive Marion Bowles and learns the military runs a parallel clone project: male clones called Castor.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Castor and the military faction that dominates the next season, and reveals Mrs. S traded Helena for it.

cliffhanger.text: Sarah has rescued Kira and blinded Rachel, but Mrs. S has secretly traded Helena to the military and the existence of male Castor clones — and a young second-generation clone named Charlotte — has just been revealed.
questions: What does the military want with Helena?
Can Sarah forgive Mrs. S once she learns of the trade?
How many Castor clones are out there, and are they hunting the Leda sisters?

characters.name: Sarah Manning
characters.line: Reunited with Kira and Cosima, still one step ahead of Dyad and now aware a whole second cloning program exists.

characters.name: Helena
characters.line: Fully switched sides to the Ledas, freshly pregnant with her own harvested embryos and just abducted by the military.

characters.name: Alison Hendrix
characters.line: Recovered from rehab, bonded with Donnie over Leekie's buried body, and reinventing herself as a suburban operator.

characters.name: Donnie Hendrix
characters.line: Exposed monitor turned accomplice; killed Leekie by accident and is now fully inside the clone conspiracy with Alison.

characters.name: Cosima Niehaus
characters.line: Sick and worsening, patched up with Kira's stem cells and clinging to the coded genome Ethan Duncan left behind.

characters.name: Delphine Cormier
characters.line: Promoted to head of clone research at Dyad and sent overseas by Rachel, separating her from Cosima.

characters.name: Rachel Duncan
characters.line: Blinded in one eye by Sarah, learned she cannot bear children, and left in Dyad custody after her own coup collapsed.

characters.name: Mrs. S (Siobhan Sadler)
characters.line: Revealed to be deeply networked in the military-adjacent underworld; sold Helena out to Paul in exchange for the Castor intel.

characters.name: Paul Dierden
characters.line: Undercover military the whole time, arranged Helena's capture with Mrs. S and left Dyad behind.

characters.name: Marion Bowles
characters.line: Dyad executive above Rachel who kept a captive Castor clone in her home and briefed Sarah on the military program.

characters.name: Mark Rollins
characters.line: Ex-Prolethean enforcer now revealed as a Castor clone; escaped Henrik's farm with pregnant Gracie.

characters.name: Kira
characters.line: Sarah's daughter, back home, now known to have accelerated healing that makes her uniquely valuable.

characters.name: Art Bell
characters.line: Fully read in on the Clone Club, working with Sarah rather than against her.

beats.label: S3 · Castor sisters and Helsinki
beats.text: Topside enforcer Ferdinand arrives to execute the Leda clones as he did in Helsinki; Sarah impersonates a broken Rachel to call him off, buying the sisters a reprieve.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes Ferdinand, the Helsinki purge precedent, and Rachel's incapacity that Sarah exploits going forward.

beats.label: S3 · Castor hunts and Castor sickness
beats.text: Castor clones Rudy and Seth hunt Sarah for original clone DNA. Cosima autopsies Seth and discovers Castor and Leda are biological siblings, both dying of matching defects.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the Castor clones as sibling threats and links both projects to a single origin.

beats.label: S3 · Alison's suburban drug empire
beats.text: Alison beats her rival Marci by taking over Ramon's drug supply with Donnie, then buys her mother's soap shop Bubbles as a laundering front while running for school trustee.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the Hendrix drug operation and Bubbles as the setting for their later storylines.

beats.label: S3 · Paul dies exposing Castor
beats.text: Paul helps Sarah escape the Castor base and reveals Dr. Virginia Coady is weaponising a Castor pathogen that sterilises women. He blows himself up with Coady's evidence.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Paul and names Coady and the pathogen as the season's real threat.

beats.label: S3 · Rachel replaced by Krystal
beats.text: Dr. Nealon smuggles a recovering Rachel out of Dyad and installs Krystal — an unaware Leda clone — in her hospital bed to fool Delphine, revealing Neolution owns everything.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Rachel from the board, introduces Krystal, and names Neolution as the real power behind Dyad and Castor.

beats.label: S3 · The original is Mrs. S's mother
beats.text: In London, Sarah learns Kendall Malone — Mrs. S's imprisoned mother — is the genetic original of both Leda and Castor, a chimera carrying two genetic lines.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Rewrites the show's origin story and puts the cure to both diseases inside the family.

beats.label: S3 · Delphine shot, Rachel's new eye
beats.text: The Clone Club celebrates Alison's election win and Delphine reconciles with Cosima — then is shot by an unseen figure. Rachel, prosthetic eye fitted, is delivered to her presumed-dead mother Susan Duncan.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up next season's two central mysteries: who shot Delphine and where Rachel and Susan are operating from.

cliffhanger.text: Neolution has been outed as the real power behind both clone projects. Delphine has been shot at point-blank range, and Rachel is captive on an unknown island with Charlotte and her supposedly dead mother Susan Duncan.
questions: Is Delphine dead, and who pulled the trigger?
Where is Rachel being held, and what does Susan Duncan want from her?
Now that the Clone Club knows Neolution runs everything, who inside their circle is still compromised?

characters.name: Sarah Manning
characters.line: Back in Iceland with Kira after her London trip revealed Neolution's structure and her family's central role in it.

characters.name: Helena
characters.line: Escaped the Castor base, killed the Prolethean-cell-turned-Castor scout Rudy, and is now living openly with the sisters, still pregnant.

characters.name: Alison Hendrix
characters.line: Won the school trustee election while secretly running a suburban drug operation out of Bubbles with Donnie.

characters.name: Donnie Hendrix
characters.line: Alison's fully committed partner in the drug trade and household protector.

characters.name: Cosima Niehaus
characters.line: Recovering thanks to Kendall's genome, reconciled with Delphine moments before Delphine was shot.

characters.name: Delphine Cormier
characters.line: Left Dyad to protect Cosima, uncovered Neolution's takeover, and was shot in a parking garage at the finale.

characters.name: Rachel Duncan
characters.line: Recovered from her eye injury, secretly extracted from Dyad by Neolution, and delivered to her mother Susan on a hidden island.

characters.name: Mrs. S (Siobhan Sadler)
characters.line: Forgiven by Sarah and now protecting her mother Kendall Malone, the genetic original for both clone lines.

characters.name: Kendall Malone
characters.line: Mrs. S's chain-smoking ex-con mother, a chimera whose DNA is the source of both Leda and Castor and the key to any cure.

characters.name: Ferdinand
characters.line: Topside cleaner who ran the Helsinki clone purge, defected after learning Neolution had infiltrated Topside, now an uneasy ally.

characters.name: Dr. Virginia Coady
characters.line: Military scientist running the Castor project and its bioweapon program, captured by Ferdinand at season's end.

characters.name: Susan Duncan
characters.line: Rachel's presumed-dead adoptive mother, alive on a private island and clearly still deep inside the science of Neolution.

characters.name: Charlotte
characters.line: The child clone from the failed second Leda batch, being raised on the island alongside a reunited Rachel.

characters.name: Krystal Goderitch
characters.line: An unaware Leda clone drugged into a coma and used to smuggle Rachel out of Dyad.

characters.name: Art Bell
characters.line: Detective still inside the police, quietly running interference for the Clone Club.

characters.name: Felix
characters.line: Sarah's foster brother, holding the loft as the sisters' base of operations.

beats.label: S4 · Beth's forgotten investigation
beats.text: Flashbacks show detective Beth, before her suicide, uncovered Neolution's cheek implants and the mask-wearing Leda hacker M.K., who now calls Sarah to warn that Neolution has found her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces M.K. and reframes Beth's death as motivated by everything Neolution is now doing to Sarah.

beats.label: S4 · A worm in Sarah's cheek
beats.text: Neolution paramedics attack Sarah believing she is M.K.; she escapes to find a biotech maggot-bot implanted in her cheek, quietly editing her DNA on Neolution's orders.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the season's ticking clock and grounds Neolution's real project in body horror.

beats.label: S4 · Brightborn and Evie Cho
beats.text: Sarah, Cosima and Donnie infiltrate the Brightborn fertility clinic and meet Evie Cho, the Neolutionist pushing gene-editing bots as therapy — and euthanising deformed newborns.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names Evie as the season's antagonist and reveals what Neolution actually wants to sell the world.

beats.label: S4 · Kendall killed, the cure lost
beats.text: Cosima and Sarah trade Kendall's genome to Susan Duncan for a cure. Evie double-crosses them, has Detective Duko burn Kendall alive, and wipes all the research.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kills the original genome, ends any easy cure, and destroys Mrs. S's mother; drives the family fracture that follows.

beats.label: S4 · Mrs. S kills Duko, Alison breaks
beats.text: Cornered by Duko into betraying Sarah to save Donnie, Alison delivers him to Mrs. S, who shoots him dead with a sniper rifle to avenge Kendall.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Confirms Mrs. S will now kill for family and traps Alison in the conspiracy at knifepoint.

beats.label: S4 · Rachel takes down Evie
beats.text: Rachel returns from the island, teams up with Sarah, and publicly destroys Evie Cho by broadcasting her admitting to Brightborn's baby-killings, then pivots to seize Neolution herself.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends Evie's arc and installs Rachel as Neolution's new operator heading into season 5.

beats.label: S4 · Westmorland is real
beats.text: Rachel stabs Susan and takes the cure. Sarah is left bleeding on the island beach as Ferdinand kidnaps Kira and Mrs. S, and Rachel gleefully prepares to meet Neolution's centuries-old founder P.T. Westmorland.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the final villain, the Kira endgame, and Rachel fully as Neolution's spokesperson.

cliffhanger.text: Rachel has betrayed Susan, hijacked the cure, and put herself in front of Neolution's founder P.T. Westmorland. Sarah is bleeding on the island while Ferdinand — now defected back to Neolution — holds Kira and Mrs. S hostage.
questions: Who is P.T. Westmorland and how is he still alive centuries later?
What does Neolution want with Kira specifically?
Can Sarah get off the island and reach her family before Rachel does?

characters.name: Sarah Manning
characters.line: Bleeding on the island after Rachel stabbed her, cut off from Kira and Mrs. S, who are now hostages of Ferdinand.

characters.name: Kira
characters.line: Sarah's daughter, whose accelerated healing has made her the centrepiece of Neolution's endgame; taken hostage with Mrs. S.

characters.name: Mrs. S (Siobhan Sadler)
characters.line: Killed Duko for her mother Kendall's murder, now captive of Ferdinand alongside Kira.

characters.name: Helena
characters.line: Living off-grid in the woods, still pregnant with twins, and just saved Alison and Donnie from a Neolution paramedic.

characters.name: Alison Hendrix
characters.line: Broken by having to sell out Sarah to save Donnie; trying to protect her family from the fallout.

characters.name: Donnie Hendrix
characters.line: Briefly jailed and threatened inside prison by Neolution; released and shaken.

characters.name: Cosima Niehaus
characters.line: Cure destroyed by Evie, now working with Susan Duncan on the island using her own eggs and Castor sperm to make a stem-cell cure.

characters.name: Delphine Cormier
characters.line: Revealed to have survived the shooting, hidden at a Neolution camp on the island, reunited with Cosima at the finale.

characters.name: Rachel Duncan
characters.line: Toppled Evie, stabbed Susan, seized the cure and Neolution's leadership, and is about to meet founder P.T. Westmorland.

characters.name: Susan Duncan
characters.line: Left bleeding on the island floor after being betrayed by the daughter she reconciled with.

characters.name: Felix
characters.line: Reconnected with newly-discovered biological half-sister Adele; helping Sarah as always.

characters.name: Art Bell
characters.line: Still the Clone Club's police contact; his partner Duko turned out to be Neolution and is dead.

characters.name: Ferdinand
characters.line: Defected back to Neolution under Rachel and now holding Kira and Mrs. S for her.

characters.name: Krystal Goderitch
characters.line: Amateur-sleuth Leda clone whose bumbling Brightborn investigation gave Sarah key intel and confirmed Delphine was alive.

characters.name: P.T. Westmorland
characters.line: Neolution's founder, presented as centuries-old, finally emerging from the shadows to meet Rachel.

beats.label: S5 · Revival on the island
beats.text: Sarah finds Cosima inside Revival, Westmorland's civilised village on the island, and escapes alone; Cosima stays to work with Neolution's science and be near a healing Delphine.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Splits the Clone Club across two fronts — the island and the city — for the final season.

beats.label: S5 · Rachel takes Kira
beats.text: Rachel demands Kira for testing; the family kidnaps her back, but M.K. is beaten to death by Ferdinand as the distraction, and Kira insists on submitting to Rachel to understand herself.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts Kira inside Neolution voluntarily and removes M.K. from the board.

beats.label: S5 · Kira's eggs for the world
beats.text: On the island, Westmorland reveals the plan: harvest Kira's eggs and implant them in 1300 surrogates to control the healing gene, and his 170-year lifespan is a lie built on children's blood.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the endgame and unmasks Westmorland as a fraud rather than a genuine immortal.

beats.label: S5 · Susan dead, Cosima flees
beats.text: Susan Duncan turns on Westmorland after learning about the children's blood and is murdered; Cosima and Charlotte incite the Revival villagers with the immortality lie and sail off the island.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Susan, breaks Neolution's island stronghold and frees Cosima to bring the truth back.

beats.label: S5 · Rachel switches sides
beats.text: Discovering her prosthetic eye is Westmorland's live camera on her, Rachel drugs Kira but tips Art off, releases her, gouges the eye out, and exposes Westmorland to his own backers.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Turns Rachel from antagonist to ally and destroys Westmorland's financial support.

beats.label: S5 · Mrs. S and Ferdinand kill each other
beats.text: Delphine, Siobhan and Ferdinand upload Rachel's stolen data to expose Neolution to the world; Ferdinand then attacks Mrs. S in her home and the two of them die together.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Mrs. S and Ferdinand and completes the public collapse of Neolution.

beats.label: S5 · Killing Westmorland, keeping the sisters
beats.text: Sarah crushes Westmorland's skull as Helena delivers her twin boys with Art's help. Months later the sisters gather at a baby shower, and Rachel hands Felix the list of all 274 Leda clones.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes the series' central threat and lands the sisters in a stable ending shape.

cliffhanger.text: Series finale — no cliffhanger. Westmorland is dead, Neolution is publicly exposed, Helena's twins are safely born, and the sisters are together at last, with a list of every Leda clone left to find and save.
questions: How many of the 274 unaware Ledas will Cosima and Delphine reach in time?
Can Sarah settle into a life with Kira and Felix now that there is no one left to run from?
What kind of mother will Helena be, raising Arthur and Donnie in Alison's garage?

characters.name: Sarah Manning
characters.line: Killed Westmorland herself and, urged by her sisters, chose to stay instead of running again.

characters.name: Kira
characters.line: Reunited with Sarah after Rachel let her go; no longer a Neolution target.

characters.name: Helena
characters.line: Delivered twin boys, Arthur and Donnie, and is raising them in the Hendrix garage surrounded by family.

characters.name: Alison Hendrix
characters.line: Back from her retreat with a new look, reconciled with Donnie, and hosting the sisters' new normal.

characters.name: Donnie Hendrix
characters.line: Out of prison and back home, still Alison's partner in everything.

characters.name: Cosima Niehaus
characters.line: Cured herself and reunited with Delphine; the two are travelling the world administering the cure to every unaware Leda.

characters.name: Delphine Cormier
characters.line: Alive and back with Cosima, working with her to cure the remaining Ledas.

characters.name: Rachel Duncan
characters.line: Broke with Neolution, cut out her surveillance eye, handed Sarah the list of all 274 Ledas, and walked away alone but free.

characters.name: Felix
characters.line: Held his art show and now carries the master list of the surviving Ledas.

characters.name: Art Bell
characters.line: Delivered Helena's twins alongside Sarah and has taken in Charlotte as his own.

characters.name: Charlotte
characters.line: The young clone rescued from the island, now living with Art.
